title: Polarization calculus and symmetric kernel over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. For abelian varieties $B,C/k$, write $\operatorname{Hom}^0_k(B,C)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(B,C)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, where homomorphisms are group-scheme homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme] and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; multiplication of rational endomorphisms is composition. There exists a normalized dual Poincare datum $(A^\vee,\mathcal P_A)$ [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. For every invertible module $N$ on $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module], its normalized translated-difference family defines a homomorphism $\phi_N:A\to A^\vee$, whose value on a geometric point $x$ is $[t_x^*N\otimes N^{-1}]$. Here $t_x$ is translation by $x$ and pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. These homomorphisms satisfy
$$\phi_{N\otimes P}=\phi_N+\phi_P,\qquad \phi_{\mathcal O_A}=0,\qquad \phi_{b^*N}=b^\vee\phi_Nb$$
for invertible modules $N,P$ and every $b\in\operatorname{End}_k(A)$. Here the dual $b^\vee:A^\vee\to A^\vee$ is the homomorphism classifying the family $(b\times1)^*\mathcal P_A$ on $A\times_kA^\vee$, with the pulled-back identity-axis trivialization; on a geometric point it sends the class of a line $Q$ to the class of $b^*Q$. Duality $b\mapsto b^\vee$ is additive and extends $\mathbf Q$-linearly to rational homomorphisms. If $L$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], $\lambda=\phi_L$ has a two-sided inverse in $\operatorname{Hom}^0_k(A^\vee,A)$, and
$$v^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}v^\vee\lambda$$
is a $\mathbf Q$-linear involution on $\operatorname{End}^0_k(A)$ reversing multiplication and fixing rational scalar multiples of the identity. If $N$ is symmetric, meaning $[-1]^*N\simeq N$, and the image of $\phi_N$ in $\operatorname{Hom}^0_k(A,A^\vee)$ is zero, then $N^{\otimes2}\simeq\mathcal O_A$. No algebraic closedness, perfection or characteristic restriction on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent auxiliary for the abelian endomorphism-span input: I §8 Proposition 8.4 and Remark 8.5 (kernel and inversion), pp.35–40 (dual and normalized differences), §9 (duality), Lemma 10.6 (torsion-free homomorphisms), and §14 opening Rosati formula; the arbitrary-field assembly is explained in the report.

proof.text: Regard $A$ as a group algebraic space via [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]; it is commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative], and proper, smooth and of finite presentation over the Noetherian base $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its geometric fibres are abelian varieties by [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension]. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus] over the locally Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its dual is a proper smooth group algebraic space with geometrically connected abelian fibres. It is separated and locally of finite type, so [lem-sfb-locally-separated-group-space-scheme] represents it by a group scheme. The same characterization makes that scheme an abelian variety. The ordinary-line/etale-line equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-etale-invertible-comparison] identifies its universal module and rigidification with a normalized dual datum in [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. The tensor-sum clause of that datum is the pullback of the second biadditivity $(1,m_{A^\vee})^*\mathcal P_A\simeq p_{12}^*\mathcal P_A\otimes p_{13}^*\mathcal P_A$ along $1\times(f,g)$. The cited Poincare calculus gives, for every $N$, the group homomorphism classifying $N_N$, its geometric-point formula, and dual homomorphisms classifying pulled-back Poincare families. All these statements apply over $k$ itself.

source.place: I §8, pp.36–40 and §9 opening; arbitrary-field assembly through the existing relative Poincare theorem.

proof.text: Write $c:A\times A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $e: \operatorname{Spec}k\to A$. The definition is $N_N=m^*N\otimes p_1^*N^{-1}\otimes p_2^*N^{-1}\otimes c^*e^*N$. Distributing pullback over tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] gives $N_{N\otimes P}\simeq N_N\otimes N_P$ and $N_{\mathcal O_A}\simeq\mathcal O_{A\times A}$, preserving the identity rigidifications. The universal property and tensor group law of [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum] therefore give $\phi_{N\otimes P}=\phi_N+\phi_P$ and $\phi_{\mathcal O_A}=0$.

source.place: I §8, normalized difference on pp.39–40; tensor identities written out by N8.

proof.text: For $b\in\operatorname{End}_k(A)$, the group-homomorphism identities $m(b\times b)=bm$ and $be=e$ give $N_{b^*N}\simeq(b\times b)^*N_N$, using pullback composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] and tensor compatibility [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. The defining identity for $b^\vee$ from [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus] identifies the latter family with $(1\times b^\vee\phi_Nb)^*\mathcal P_A$. Both identifications preserve the axis rigidification. Uniqueness in [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum] proves $\phi_{b^*N}=b^\vee\phi_Nb$. Restricting the defining identity for $b^\vee$ to a geometric point gives the stated class $[b^*Q]$.

source.place: I §9 opening, p.41; substitution in the normalized difference of §8 p.40.

proof.text: For $f,g:B\to C$, apply the first-variable biadditivity of $\mathcal P_C$ from [lem-sfb-abelian-space-poincare-calculus] along $(f,g,1)$: the family for $(f+g)^\vee$ is the tensor of the families for $f^\vee$ and $g^\vee$. The representing tensor law gives $(f+g)^\vee=f^\vee+g^\vee$. Likewise functorial pullback gives $(hf)^\vee=f^\vee h^\vee$, and identity pullback gives $1^\vee=1$, by uniqueness of classifiers. The comparisons are those of [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. An additive map extends uniquely to a $\mathbf Q$-linear map on $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ by $f\otimes q\mapsto f^\vee\otimes q$; the tensor relations are respected because the map is additive. The composition identity extends by bilinearity. Thus duality fixes rational multiples of the identity.

source.place: I Remark 8.5, p.36 and §9 opening, p.41; rational extension by the tensor relations.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ample-line-polarization-isogeny] to the ample line $L$, obtaining that $\lambda=\phi_L$ is an isogeny over $k$. By [lem-sfb-simple-isogeny-decomposition], choose $g:A^\vee\to A$ and $n>0$ with $g\lambda=[n]_A$ and $\lambda g=[n]_{A^\vee}$. Then $\mu=n^{-1}g$ satisfies $\mu\lambda=1_A$ and $\lambda\mu=1_{A^\vee}$ in the rational Hom groups. This constructs the required two-sided inverse.

source.place: I Remark 8.6 p.36 and §14 opening p.61.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-poincare-biduality] to identify $A$ with $A^{\vee\vee}$ through $\delta_A$. The normalized difference $N_L$ is invariant under swapping its two factors: $m$ is commutative [lem-sc-av-commutative] and its two projection factors exchange. The bidual Poincare identity and the definition of $\lambda^\vee$ give $(1\times\lambda^\vee\delta_A)^*\mathcal P_A\simeq s^*(1\times\lambda)^*\mathcal P_A=s^*N_L\simeq N_L$ on $A\times A$, where $s$ swaps factors. Each comparison respects the first identity-axis rigidification: on that axis the evaluation of a line against its inverse cancels. The universal property [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum] gives $\lambda^\vee\delta_A=\lambda$. Thus the required symmetry of the polarization is proved from the symmetric family, without an assumption that $L$ itself is symmetric.

source.place: I §8 biduality pp.37–38 and normalized difference p.40; symmetry calculation for §14.

proof.text: Set $v^\dagger=\mu v^\vee\lambda$. Step 4 and distributivity of composition give $\mathbf Q$-linearity. Also $(vw)^\dagger=\mu w^\vee v^\vee\lambda=(\mu w^\vee\lambda)(\mu v^\vee\lambda)=w^\dagger v^\dagger$, inserting $\lambda\mu=1$. For a rational scalar $a$, $(a1)^\dagger=\mu(a1)\lambda=a1$.

source.place: I §14 opening p.61; algebraic identities expanded by N8.

proof.text: Dualizing both inverse identities gives $\mu^\vee\lambda^\vee=1$ and $\lambda^\vee\mu^\vee=1$, so $\mu^\vee=\delta_A\mu$ by step 6 and uniqueness of a two-sided inverse. Naturality from [lem-sfb-abelian-poincare-biduality] gives $v^{\vee\vee}\delta_A=\delta_Av$, also for rational $v$ by linearity. Consequently $(v^\dagger)^\dagger=\mu\lambda^\vee v^{\vee\vee}\mu^\vee\lambda=\mu\lambda^\vee v^{\vee\vee}\delta_A=\mu\lambda^\vee\delta_Av=v$. This proves involutivity over $k$.

source.place: I §14 opening p.61; bidual calculation replacing the equivalent Tate-pairing calculation in the source.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free], $\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,A^\vee)$ has a finite integer basis and hence is torsion-free: in basis coordinates $nh=0$ forces every integer coefficient to be zero when $n>0$. Apply [lem-trf-torsionfree-rationalization-injective]. If the rational image of $\phi_N$ is zero, then $\phi_N=0$ as a genuine group-scheme homomorphism.

source.place: I Lemma 10.6 p.45 (torsion-free Hom), with the stronger existing Theorem 10.15 node; rational injection.

proof.text: The Poincare classifier now gives $N_N\simeq\mathcal O_{A\times A}$, since $(1\times0)^*\mathcal P_A$ is trivial on the other identity axis [def-sfb-abelian-dual-poincare-datum]. Pull back along $j:A\to A\times A$, $j(x)=(x,-x)$. In the formula for $N_N$, $mj=e\circ p$, $p_1j=1$ and $p_2j=[-1]$, with $p:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus $j^*N_N\simeq(p^*e^*N)^{\otimes2}\otimes N^{-1}\otimes([-1]^*N)^{-1}$ by pullback composition and tensor compatibility [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition, lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. The constant line $p^*e^*N$ is trivial because a one-dimensional vector space over $k$ has a basis. If $[-1]^*N\simeq N$, cancellation gives $N^{\otimes2}\simeq\mathcal O_A$. Every isomorphism in this step is over $k$, so no descent of a geometric trivialization is assumed; the argument works unchanged in characteristic two and dimension zero.

source.place: I Proposition 8.4(c) and Remark 8.5 p.36; direct normalized-family proof over k written by N8.
